question: A closure search calibrates three direction arms; the map asks for q50 alone, so the two are different day identities and the same calendar day was calibrated twice. May a three-variant day answer a q50-only request — that is, is the median arm the SAME artifact whether or not the stress arms were built alongside it? If not, sharing the bytes would be a silent approximation.
argument: q50 is solved first and its integer population is then frozen as a hard equality for q10/q90, so the stress arms are downstream of it; each arm is published from its own solution through the same writer, whose per-day draw streams are day-local (stage B). Nothing in the q50 path reads a stress arm. This record exists because that argument, however sound, is not evidence.

case.why: a clean date with no stored generation, so both builds start cold from the same candidate pool

method: Build 2027-05-26 twice on identical inputs — once q50-only, once with --direction-stress-variants — and compare the day-library entry the second build stores under the q50-only identity against the entry the first build stored. Artifacts are gzipped with a wall-clock header, so the comparison is of DECOMPRESSED bytes. Then delete both, rebuild three-variant only, and ask for the date as the map does, to check the hit is real and publishes the same demand.
fit_timings_note: fit.json carries four wall-clock durations under timings_s (prepare_shared, interval_solving_shared, integer_repair_shared, route_publish). They differ between ANY two runs, including two q50-only runs, so they are not evidence of a different result. Every substantive field — vehicles, geh_ok/geh_total/geh_pct, achieved, unserviceable_edges, bound_violations, relaxed_bound_violations, inactive_sensor_integer_stability, inactive_sensor_observability, sensor_anchor_contract, purpose_allocation, purpose_allocation_summary, relaxation_summary — is identical.

digests.note: sha256 of the DECOMPRESSED artifact, produced by the q50-only build and reproduced exactly by the three-variant build's subset entry

end_to_end.method: library emptied for the date, three-variant build run, then the same q50-only request the web recalibration makes

scope_and_limits: pool_composition stays part of the identity: a date calibrated inside a window that also contains a weekend is a different (equally correct) result and is NOT shared with a single-day request. Only the variant axis is bridged.
The subset is written when a day is CALIBRATED. A three-variant day that is itself served from the library does not backfill one, so days stored before this change keep needing their own q50 build.
Direction is one-way by construction: a q50-only day cannot answer a three-variant request, which needs arms it never solved.
Cost: about 3.5 MB per stored day on top of the roughly 13 MB the three-variant entry already occupies.

provenance.dirty_note: the working tree carried in-progress direction-split edits to build_sumo_demand.py, demand/calibration.py, traffic_sim/demand/pfe.py and run_scenario.py. Both halves of the comparison ran against the SAME tree, which is what an identity claim needs; the record is not a claim about any committed revision.
